posts.author: Markus
posts.body: The lights along the Emajõgi made the walk home worth taking the long way round.
posts.imageAlt: Evening lights and autumn trees reflected in the Emajõgi in Tartu

posts.author: Kertu
posts.body: Finally got the fetch flow straight: request the JSON, wait for the response, parse it, then build the posts in the page.

posts.author: Aino
posts.body: Coffee and a few pages of notes before the afternoon practical. This little break helped.
posts.imageAlt: A warm café opening onto a cobbled old-town street in Tartu

posts.author: Rasmus
posts.body: Small win today: the feed is coming from JSON now, so adding another post doesn't mean copying another block of HTML.
posts.imageAlt: A study desk with a laptop, notebook, and coffee beside an autumn city window

posts.author: Liis
posts.body: If fetch fails when you open the page as a file, start a local server with python -m http.server. That fixed it for me.

posts.author: Markus
posts.body: Tartu looked especially calm from the riverbank tonight. I needed the fresh air after sitting at my desk all afternoon.
posts.imageAlt: Tartu riverside buildings and lights reflected in the water at dusk

posts.author: Kertu
posts.body: Used textContent for the post text instead of building HTML strings. The rendering code is much easier to follow now.

posts.author: Aino
posts.body: Went out for coffee after finishing the first draft of the responsive layout. A good reason to close the laptop for a bit.
posts.imageAlt: Café tables along a cobbled old-town street in Tartu

posts.author: Rasmus
posts.body: Quick reminder to check the page at phone width too. A layout that looks fine on a laptop can still overflow on mobile.

posts.author: Liis
posts.body: One more thing checked off. Saving the work now and calling it a day before I find another tiny CSS detail to change.
posts.imageAlt: A laptop and handwritten notes on a desk in soft morning light
